title: DMart Sells More but Keeps Less of Every ₹100. Why?

beats.say: Out of every hundred rupees D Mart sells, how much does it keep? Not twenty rupees. Not ten. Less than six, and that is before income tax. In the same three months last year, it kept six rupees and eighteen paise. This time, five rupees and sixty two. Fifty six paise went missing. That sounds like nothing. But it is almost a tenth of everything D Mart had left. So who took it?

beats.say: Why does that matter? A new store costs a lot to build. But the company's books do not count that cost in one go. They spread it over many years, one slice every year, like a shopkeeper counting a new delivery van as it wears out. So every new store adds a slice to every future year.
